title: LED Inspection - Overlay Shift Detection on Puma 9900
subtitle: Post-CMP Quality Validation for 65nm Node Manufacturing
author: Lisa Johansson

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Puma 9900 system to detect and classify Overlay Shift defects during post-cmp inspection at the 65nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 200mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Overlay Shift defects that are critical to yield at the 65nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Puma 9900 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Puma 9900
- Inspection Type: LED Inspection
- Target Defect: Overlay Shift
- Process Step: Post-CMP
- Wafer Size: 200mm
- Technology Node: 65nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Puma 9900 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for post-cmp monitoring in the 65nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Puma 9900
Software Version: v14.0.740
Recipe: LED_INSPECTION_65nm_POST_CMP
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Medium (88 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 4mm
Sampling Plan: 9-point sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Puma 9900 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'LED Inspection' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Overlay Shift defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 65nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 103 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 90% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±0.7% for LED Inspection
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.94 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-05-08
Wafers Tested: 43
Total Defects Found: 1378
Defect Density: 438.63 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 5.9%
Capture Rate: 91.4%
Test Duration: 83 minutes
System Uptime: 98.5%

Result Classification: FAIL
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Puma 9900 demonstrated below-target performance in detecting Overlay Shift at the 65nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Minor calibration drift was detected after extended run; re-calibration resolved the issue.

e) Statistical process control charts showed stable performance over the test period.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
The following corrective actions are recommended:

1. Re-tune detection algorithm thresholds for Overlay Shift at 65nm node.
2. Schedule follow-up test after recipe optimization.
3. Escalate to R&D for algorithm enhancement if re-tuning does not resolve sensitivity gap.
